title: What Do You Do? (Work & Study)

expressions.meaning: O que você faz? (qual é o seu trabalho)
expressions.example: What do you do? — I fix GPS systems on tractors.

expressions.expr: I work from Monday to Friday.
expressions.meaning: Eu trabalho de segunda a sexta.
expressions.example: I work from Monday to Friday at GPS Tronic.
I work all day and I study agronomy at night.
I read manuals, but I don't speak much English.

sentences: What do you do?
I fix GPS systems on tractors.
I study agronomy at night.
He checks the antennas every day.
My boss talks to the customers.
Does Pedro work with you?
Yes, he does. He works here.
I read manuals in English.

grammar.title: Padrão: falar da sua rotina (work / works)
rules: Para I, you, we, they o verbo fica puro: I work, I study, we fix.
Para he, she, it o verbo ganha -s ou -es: He works, he checks, he fixes, he studies.
⚠️ Na pergunta (Do/Does) e na negativa (don't/doesn't), o verbo volta a ficar puro: Does Pedro work here?
A resposta curta repete o do/does: Yes, I do. / Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.

quiz.a: He checks the antennas every day.
opts: He checks the antennas every day.
He check the antennas every day.
He is check the antennas every day.
He checking the antennas every day.
quiz.why: Com he, she ou it na rotina, o verbo ganha -s: checks.
O -s já está no Does, então o verbo work fica puro.
Verbos terminados em -x, -ch, -sh, -s ou -o ganham -es com he/she/it.

opts: I am study agronomy at night.
quiz.why: Com I o verbo fica puro (study), e 'à noite' é sempre at night.

quiz.q: Jack pergunta: "Do you like your job?". Você gosta. Responda:
quiz.why: A resposta curta em inglês repete o auxiliar da pergunta: Do you...? -> Yes, I do.

speak: What do you do?
I fix GPS systems on tractors.
I study agronomy at night.
He checks the antennas every day.
Does Pedro work with you?

title: Every Day at Six (Daily Routine)

expressions.expr: What time does the shift start?
expressions.example: What time does the shift start? — It starts at six.

expressions.expr: I always wake up at five.
expressions.example: I always wake up at five in the morning.
How long is the break? — One hour.
Sometimes we work on Saturday, but we never work on Sunday.

sentences: What time does the shift start?
It starts at six o'clock.
I always wake up at five.
Usually I have breakfast at home.
Lunch is at half past eleven in the shed.
How long is the break?
In the harvest we work until eight.
We never work on Sunday.

grammar.title: Padrão: frequência (always, usually, sometimes, never)
rules: always (sempre), usually (geralmente), sometimes (às vezes) e never (nunca) vêm ANTES do verbo normal: I always wake up at five.
Mas com o verbo to be (am, is, are), eles vêm DEPOIS: He is never late.
⚠️ never já é negativo — nunca use don't junto com never: We never work on Sunday.
every + dia não usa preposição: every Monday, every day.

rows: I always wake up at five.

quiz.a: I always wake up at five.
opts: I always wake up at five.
I wake up always at five.
I always wakes up at five.
I am always wake up at five.
quiz.why: always vem antes do verbo normal (wake up).

opts: We don't never work on Sunday.
quiz.why: never já nega sozinho (sem don't), e dias da semana usam on.
Com o verbo to be (is), o never vem depois do verbo.
How long pergunta duração de tempo; how far pergunta distância.

quiz.a: In the harvest we work until eight.
opts: In the harvest we work until eight.
In the harvest we work to eight.
In the harvest we works until eight.
On the harvest we work until eight.
quiz.why: until marca até que horário uma ação continua.

speak: What time does the shift start?
I always wake up at five.
How long is the break?
In the harvest we work until eight.
We never work on Sunday.

title: Do You Like Soccer? (Sports & Free Time)

expressions.example: Do you like soccer? — Yes, I love it!

expressions.meaning: Sim, eu adoro! — o 'it' nunca some
expressions.example: Do you like handball? — Yes, I love it!
Pedro doesn't like soccer. He prefers fishing.

expressions.expr: What do you do on weekends?
expressions.meaning: O que você faz nos fins de semana?
expressions.example: What do you do on weekends? — I play handball on Sundays.

sentences: Do you like soccer?
Yes, I love it!
I also play handball on Sundays.
Handball is my favorite sport.
Does Pedro like soccer too?
No, he doesn't. He prefers fishing.
We go to the farm show every year.
I live in the countryside.

grammar.title: Padrão: falar do que você gosta (like, love, prefer)
rules: ⚠️ like não leva 'of': diga I like soccer, nunca I like of soccer.
Em inglês o objeto nunca fica vazio depois de like ou love: Yes, I love it! (nunca só 'Yes, I love').
Depois de like, love e prefer, se vier outro verbo, use -ing: I like playing soccer, He prefers fishing.
Com he/she/it: Does Pedro like...? -> Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.

quiz.why: like já significa 'gostar de' — nunca use of depois dele.

quiz.q: Jack pergunta: "Do you like soccer?". Qual resposta está certa?
quiz.why: love precisa de complemento em inglês: I love it!
Com Pedro (he) usamos Does, e o verbo like fica sem -s.
Com he o verbo ganha -s (prefers) e a atividade vem com -ing (fishing).

opts: Which is your favorite of sport?
quiz.why: favorite já significa 'o preferido', sem most.

speak: Do you like soccer?
Yes, I love it!
I also play handball on Sundays.
He doesn't like it. He prefers fishing.
What do you do on weekends?

title: Country Music, Movies & Friends

expressions.meaning: Eu também! — concorda com frase afirmativa
expressions.example: I like country music. — Me too!
What music do you like? — I like Brazilian country music.

expressions.expr: I listen to music in the tractor.
expressions.meaning: Eu ouço música no trator. — listen pede TO
expressions.example: I always listen to music in the tractor cab.

expressions.meaning: Qual é o seu filme favorito?
expressions.example: What's your favorite movie? — I love Fast and Furious.

sentences: What music do you like?
I like Brazilian country music.
Me too! I listen to country music every day.
I listen to the radio in the truck.
I also watch movies at night.
Do you like fast cars?
Yes, I do! I like them too.
There is a big festival in our town.

grammar.title: Padrão: also, too e me too
rules: also e too significam 'também', mas mudam de lugar na frase.
also vai no MEIO da frase, antes do verbo: I also play handball. / I also watch movies.
too vai no FIM da frase: I like country music too.
Para concordar rápido com alguém na conversa, diga apenas: Me too! (Eu também!).

rows: I listen to music in the cab.

quiz.why: also entra no meio da frase, antes do verbo principal.

opts: I like country music also too.
quiz.why: too vai sempre no final da frase.

quiz.q: Jack diz: "I love fast cars!". Você também gosta. O que responde?
quiz.why: Me too! é a resposta natural para concordar com uma frase afirmativa.

quiz.a: I listen to music in the truck.
opts: I listen to music in the truck.
I listen music in the truck.
I hear to music in the truck.
I listening to music in the truck.
quiz.why: O verbo listen sempre pede a preposição to antes do que você ouve: listen to music.

quiz.a: Do you watch series at night?
opts: Do you watch series at night?
Do you watches series at night?
Are you watch series at night?
Do you watch series in the night?
quiz.why: Do you + verbo puro (watch), e 'à noite' é at night.

speak: What music do you like?
I like Brazilian country music.
Me too! I listen to music in the truck.
I also watch movies on weekends.
What's your favorite movie?

title: Can You Drive a Tractor?

expressions.example: Can you drive a tractor? — Yes, I can.

expressions.expr: No, I can't. I don't have a license.
expressions.meaning: Não, não posso. Não tenho habilitação.
expressions.example: Can you drive the sprayer? — No, I can't. I don't have a license.
Can I use your phone? — Of course!
I speak a little English, but I can learn fast.

sentences: Can you drive a tractor?
Yes, I can. I drive every day.
Can you load the truck?
Yes, I can. It's easy.
I can't drive the sprayer.
He can calibrate the GPS very well.
Can you help me with these bags?
Can I use your phone, please?

grammar.title: Padrão: can e can't (habilidade e pedidos)
rules: Depois de can e can't o verbo vem sempre puro: sem to e sem -s (I can drive, He can drive).
Para perguntar, coloque Can no começo da frase, sem usar do/does: Can you plant soybeans?
A resposta curta repete o can: Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
Can you...? pede um favor para outra pessoa; Can I...? pede permissão para você fazer algo.

rows: Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

quiz.q: "Ele sabe calibrar o GPS muito bem."
quiz.a: He can calibrate the GPS very well.
opts: He can calibrate the GPS very well.
He cans calibrate the GPS very well.
He can calibrates the GPS very well.
He can to calibrate the GPS very well.
quiz.why: can não muda com he, e o verbo depois dele fica puro (calibrate).

opts: I don't can drive the sprayer.
I no can drive the sprayer.
I can't to drive the sprayer.
quiz.why: A negativa de can é can't — nunca use don't antes de can.
Na pergunta, o próprio Can vai para o início da frase, sem Do.

quiz.q: Jack pergunta: "Can you load the truck?". Você sabe. Responda:
quiz.why: Pergunta com Can responde com can: Yes, I can.

quiz.q: Você quer usar o computador da oficina. Como pede licença?
opts: Do I can use the computer?
quiz.why: Can I...? pede permissão para você mesmo fazer algo.

speak: Can you drive a tractor?
Yes, I can. I drive every day.
I can't drive the sprayer.
Can you help me with the truck?
Can I use your phone, please?

title: The Weather Today (Sun, Rain & Frost)

expressions.example: What's the weather like today? — It's sunny and hot.

expressions.expr: It's too windy for the sprayer.
expressions.meaning: Está ventando demais para o pulverizador.
expressions.example: We can't spray now. It's too windy for the sprayer.

expressions.expr: Does it rain a lot here?
expressions.example: Does it rain a lot here in January? — Yes, it does.
The soil is very dry. The crop needs rain.

sentences: What's the weather like today?
It's sunny and very hot.
It's too hot at noon.
It's too windy for the sprayer today.
The field is too wet for the tractor.
Does it rain a lot in summer?
Frost is bad for the corn.
The soil is dry. We need rain!

grammar.title: Padrão: It's + clima e a diferença entre very e too
rules: Frases sobre o clima sempre começam com It's: It's hot, It's sunny, It's cold at night.
very significa 'muito' (intenso, mas normal): It's very hot today.
too significa 'demais' (passou do limite, atrapalha o trabalho): It's too wet for the tractor.
Para falar de chuva como rotina, rain é verbo com it: It rains a lot in January. / Does it rain in July?

opts: How much is the weather today?
quiz.why: Diga What's the weather like? ou How's the weather? — nunca misture How com like.

quiz.a: It's too windy for the sprayer.
opts: It's too windy for the sprayer.
Is too windy for the sprayer.
It's too much windy for the sprayer.
It has too windy for the sprayer.
quiz.why: Clima começa com It's, e antes de adjetivo (windy) usamos too, sem much.

quiz.a: It rains a lot in January.
opts: It rains a lot in January.
It's rain a lot in January.
It rain a lot on January.
quiz.why: Com it no presente simples, o verbo rain ganha -s (It rains), e meses usam in.

quiz.q: "A geada é ruim para o milho."
quiz.a: Frost is bad for the corn.
opts: Frost is bad for the corn.
Drought is bad for the corn.
Sunny is bad for the corn.
Warm is bad for the corn.
quiz.why: Frost é geada; drought é seca.

quiz.a: The field is too wet today.
opts: The field is too wet today.
The field is too dry today.
The field are too wet today.
The field is very much wet today.
quiz.why: wet = molhado/encharcado; too wet = molhado demais.

speak: What's the weather like today?
It's sunny and very hot.
It's too windy for the sprayer.
Does it rain a lot in summer?
The soil is dry. We need rain!

title: GPS & Screens in the Cab

expressions.example: Turn on the screen and check the GPS signal.
Look at the screen — there is no signal.

expressions.expr: Check the cable on the roof.
expressions.example: Check the cable on the roof of the cab.
Great! The autopilot is working now!

sentences: Turn on the screen, please.
Press the green button.
The receiver is on the roof of the cab.
There is no satellite signal.
Check the connector and the fuse.
The battery voltage is low.
Set the A-B line on the map.
Great! The autopilot is working now.

grammar.title: Padrão: dar instruções passo a passo (Turn on, Check, Press)
rules: Para dar instruções diretas na oficina ou no suporte, comece a frase direto com o verbo puro: Turn on the screen. / Check the fuse.
Para deixar a instrução educada, coloque please no começo ou no fim: Press the green button, please.
Para avisar o que NÃO fazer, comece com Don't + verbo puro: Don't touch that wire!
turn on = ligar · turn off = desligar.

opts: To turn on the screen, please.
quiz.why: Turn on = ligar (Turn off = desligar). Instruções começam com o verbo puro.
Para dizer 'não faça', usamos sempre Don't + verbo puro.

opts: It has no satellite signal here.
quiz.why: O 'tem' de existir é There is / There are.

quiz.q: Onde fica o receptor (globo) do GPS no trator?
quiz.a: On the roof of the cab.
opts: On the roof of the cab.
quiz.why: roof = teto; cab = cabine. Em cima tocando a superfície = on the roof.
autopilot é singular (it) -> is working.

speak: Turn on the screen, please.
Press the green button.
There is no satellite signal.
Check the connector and the fuse.
The autopilot is working now!

title: Trucks, Tires & the Road

expressions.example: Stop the truck! We have a flat tire.

expressions.expr: The fuel tank is almost empty.
expressions.meaning: O tanque de combustível está quase vazio.
expressions.example: We need diesel. The fuel tank is almost empty.

expressions.meaning: Qual a distância até a fazenda?
expressions.example: How far is the farm? — It's ten kilometers from here.

expressions.expr: Drive slowly on the dirt road.
expressions.meaning: Dirija devagar na estrada de terra.
expressions.example: It rained yesterday. Drive slowly on the dirt road.

sentences: Stop the truck! We have a flat tire.
Do we have a spare tire?
Can you help me change the tire?
The fuel tank is almost empty.
Is there a gas station near here?
How far is the soybean farm?
It's ten kilometers from the gate.
Drive slowly on the dirt road.

grammar.title: Padrão: How far (distância) e adjetivos opostos (full × empty)
rules: Para perguntar distância, use sempre How far is...?: How far is the workshop?
Para responder com a distância a partir de um ponto, use from: It's two kilometers from the gate.
Estrada em inglês usa a preposição on: on the highway, on the dirt road (nunca in the road).
Pneu furado em inglês é flat tire (pneu murcho/plano), nunca broken tire.

quiz.q: "A carreta está com um pneu furado."
quiz.a: The trailer has a flat tire.
opts: The trailer has a flat tire.
The trailer have a flat tire.
The trailer has a broken tire.
The trailer is a flat tire.
quiz.why: trailer é singular (it -> has), e pneu furado em inglês é flat tire.

opts: How much distance is the farm?
How many far is the farm?
quiz.why: How far pergunta distância; How long pergunta tempo.
Estradas e ruas levam a preposição on: on the dirt road.
empty = vazio (full = cheio).

quiz.a: It's ten kilometers from the gate.
opts: It's ten kilometers from the gate.
It's ten kilometers of the gate.
It's ten kilometer from the gate.
Has ten kilometers from the gate.
quiz.why: Distância a partir de um ponto usa from: ten kilometers from the gate.

speak: We have a flat tire.
The fuel tank is almost empty.
How far is the farm?
It's ten kilometers from the gate.
Drive slowly on the dirt road.
